_comment: PIPELINES ARE SEEDED NOW, AND THEY DELIBERATELY WERE NOT BEFORE.
The root .mj-sync.json used to say pipelines are per-deployment data rather than vocabulary, and
that was the right call while installing the app and configuring it were the same act. The dev->test
process changed the premise: 'install the app and test it' is now the workflow, and an app that
installs with no pipeline is an app where nobody can create a deal or render a board column. A
default nobody wants is cheaper to change than a blocker nobody expected.
THE COMPANY IS THE AWKWARD PART. A pipeline serves the companies it is linked to through
PipelineCompany, and a pipeline with no link offers no company a deal can sell as -- but companies
are MJ core data that belong to the deployment, not to this app. So each seeded pipeline carries one
related PipelineCompany row linking it to 'Default Company' (seeded by companies/). A deployment with
a real company should link its companies and retire (IsActive = 0) or rename that one;
scripts/seed-demo-data.sh does exactly that for local development. The link rows carry no IsActive,
so a push creates them active (the column default) but never re-activates one a deployment retired.
Their IDs match the ones the PipelineCompany migration gives the backfilled Default Company links, so
a push on an upgraded host updates those rows instead of colliding with them on the unique pair.
OTHER COMPANIES GET LINKS, NOT ROWS HERE (#327). Run the Sales.LinkDefaultPipelineToCompanies Action
after install, and again after adding a company: it links the IsDefault pipeline to every company
with no link to it.
This is the ONLY place sales' metadata reaches into MJ core data. It is worth knowing that, which
is why it is written here rather than assumed.
